canonical.title: Depth First Search of a Graph

narrative.title: The Corridor-to-the-End Inspection
narrative.scenario: A tunnel inspector starts at junction 0 and always takes the first unexplored tunnel ahead of her, following corridors to their dead ends before backtracking to the last junction with options left. Her hand-written log — one entry per junction, in the order first entered — is the depth-first record of the cave system.
narrative.inputFormat: An adjacency list adj for a connected undirected graph — adj[i] lists the neighbours of vertex i.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the DFS order starting from vertex 0, exploring neighbours in the order they appear in each list.
constraints: The graph is connected and undirected

testCases.explanation: The walk dives 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3, backtracks, then finishes with 4.
Each neighbour list is consumed left to right; 4 only fires after 3 is exhausted.

hintLevels: Level 1: Go as deep as possible on the first choice before ever considering the second.
Level 2: Log the node when entered, mark visited, then recurse into each unvisited neighbour in list order.
Level 3: Deep graphs can blow the call stack — an explicit stack or raised recursion limit keeps it safe.
